result.title: DiSARM: Diverse and Surprising Association Rule Mining with Large Language Models
result.summary: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) aims to discover informative patterns in large datasets. For transactional data, Association Rule Mining (ARM) is an established approach that facilitates EDA by efficiently generating candidate patterns. Beyond efficient mining, identifying informative rules has also been extensively studied through both objective and subjective interestingness measures. Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) offer new opportunities for assessing subjective interestingness using world knowledge. Nevertheless, relying solely on LLMs raises concerns about scalability and statistical reliability. Building on prior ARM research, we propose a hybrid framework, DiSARM, that leverages the world knowledge of LLMs to assess the subjective interestingness of rules, while maintaining statistical reliability and promoting diversity among the selected rules. Across three transactional datasets, experiments demonstrate that DiSARM effectively combines statistical reliability with surprise and diversity, offering a promising approach to ADE from transactional data.

AI.brief_summary: 提出混合框架 DiSARM，用 LLM 的世界知识评估关联规则的主观有趣性（惊讶度），同时保持统计可靠性与规则多样性，用于事务数据的探索性分析。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作属于表格/事务型关联规则挖掘与 EDA 筛选，不涉及多模态或视觉推理，也没有可核查的 latent 状态、证据使用或停止决策线索，与 LVR 研究主线缺少实质联系。
